what: Sailor's rulings on lines — the closed form's labelled examples. Every run shows them to the model as ruled cases; each entry is one line he has scored or corrected, with his reason. Add by telling Claude (or by hand). The relational test: Parameters/02_Protocols/Diatribe_Derivation_Protocol_Revision.md, Step 3 codified (2026-11-05).

rows.why: faces the object — the tradeoff between spending here and bombs abroad — but it's a campaign line built to win the room; the line is scored, not the man's reputation

rows.quote: she had the opportunity and the power to introduce a war powers resolution herself, and she didn't — and that's why those nine votes didn't matter
rows.why: Sailor's grounding proof: the same conclusion as 'those votes are meaningless', grounded in a checkable mechanism of her record — she can answer it, the audience can check it — so it cools from #28 to coalition. Grounding a pre-emption in a mechanism moves it back toward #1 or out of the patterns.

principles.name: reported speech
principles.rule: When a speaker passes on someone else's view, it depends on how he presents it. If he affirms its logic, score it as his own. If he presents it as a specimen (a barometer, an example of what others believe), score his framing of it, not the view.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-11-04: his 2024 Trump friend's year of Epstein and 'Israel controlling Trump', offered as 'a good barometer'

principles.name: the self-settled wager
principles.rule: When a speaker sets a test of his own (a bet, 'wake me up when that changes') and then pays it out himself before it can be applied ('even if there were, I don't care anymore'), the line is closed: 'even if' answers every reply in advance. Settling your own test is capital spent. The object is sacrificed to keep the reaction; the line leaves z (shadow). Pattern #29.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-02-28, the bet settled early (crystal line 20)

principles.name: restated record
principles.rule: A speaker's claim about his own past ('I always said', 'I was skeptical from the start') is a dated-record claim: check it against the set. If the earlier lines bear it out, it is an open statement (fluid). If they contradict it, it is an argument built to reposition him in front of the audience (working, coalition) and carries #8, the past revised to fit the present. The set decides the tier, not the words.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-03-06 and 2026-08-28 (crystal lines 21, 25) against his June–July 2025 lines
